notes: Read all three units, complete foreign-assistance context, all eleven candidates and the review. Resolved the antecedent to U.S. foundations, educational institutions, faith groups and charitable individuals; anchored the fifty-year interval to 2016; named the U.S. strategy, program and Obama administration; preserved radical social agenda and best track record as Republican evaluations; and identified the Republican Party and the course it pledged to reverse.

claims.claim_text: Any tax-code revision should weigh the essential international-development role of U.S. foundations, educational institutions, faith groups and charitable individuals.
During the fifty years preceding 2016, U.S. private overseas investment is said to have exceeded aid many times over.
The U.S. development strategy should build on Republican use of foreign aid to catalyze private investment and expertise against global challenges.
Republicans judge the Obama administration to have compromised the U.S. foreign-aid program by imposing what they call a radical social agenda on recipients, especially Africans.
Republicans allege that the Obama administration excluded faith-based aid groups because those groups would not conform to that agenda.
Republicans assess faith-based groups as having the strongest development record.
The Republican Party pledges to reverse the Obama administration's exclusionary foreign-aid course.
The Republican Party would encourage greater involvement by the most effective aid organizations.
